data.title: Decline in U.S. diesel prices likely to continue, Energy Secretary says
data.description:
U.S. diesel prices should continue to decline from record highs as refined products from the Persian Gulf return to the market and unsanctioned Russian diesel adds to downward pressure on prices, U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said Thursday.

"The trajectory we're on right now is downward for the foreseeable future," although the path depends on nothing "big or bad" happening, Wright told The Wall Street Journal in an interview at the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation conference in Warsaw.

Even as no Russian diesel has actually arrived in the U.S. and several fuel tankers have shifted course after struggling to find American buyers willing to accept the cargoes, Wright said the return of the country’s fuel to the global market puts downward pressure on the price U.S. consumers pay at the pump.

The national average price of diesel hit an all-time high of $6.53/gal in September, according to AAA, but prices have since eased to $5.93 on Thursday, while remaining well above the $3.78/gal average price from a year ago.

Wright also said U.S. diesel prices would never have risen into the $6.50s if European allies had been more proactive in releasing fuel from strategic reserves to the market.

Europe was "remarkably reluctant to release their diesel stores despite their promises to do so," Wright said, which "led to prices going higher than they should have gone."

Crude oil futures finished flat in a choppy session Thursday as tensions in the Middle East continued to be offset by improving supply.

"The oil market has become acclimated to periodic flare-ups, just as long as there is no return to all-out war," Raymond James strategist Pavel Molchanov said in a note. "With oil production among OPEC's Persian Gulf members having reached 87% of pre-war levels, the industry is gradually adapting."

A broader retreat across commodity markets and a stronger U.S. dollar are also weighing on sentiment, creating additional headwinds, analysts said.

Meanwhile, the International Energy Agency said prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could substantially reduce the world's reliance on the waterway over the next decade as Middle Eastern producers develop alternative export routes.

Front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for December delivery fell less than 0.1% to $83.21/bbl, while front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for January delivery gained less than 0.1% to $91.98/bbl, and front-month Nymex natural gas (NG1:COM) for December delivery dipped 3.1% to $3.268/MMBtu.

data.title: Northrop forgoes challenge to Boeing’s $20B+ Navy fighter win
data.description:
Northrop Grumman (NOC) won't challenge the Navy’s selection of Boeing (BA) for the F/A-XX stealth fighter program, Bloomberg News reported, removing a potential obstacle to development under a contract valued at more than $20 billion.

For investors, the decision reduces the risk of a protest-related delay to a major Boeing (BA) defense program. The award adds to Boeing’s success in securing the Air Force’s F-47 fighter contract in 2025, strengthening its position in next-generation military aviation.

Northrop said it reached its decision after reviewing information and receiving a Navy debriefing. A challenge before the Government Accountability Office could have delayed the program for months while the agency considered the dispute.

Defense consultant JJ Gentler suggested Northrop may have accepted the Navy’s explanation or prioritized its other Pentagon commitments. Those include the Sentinel nuclear missile program, with an expected cost exceeding $141 billion, and the B-21 bomber.

data.title: Nextech3D.ai outlines 30% take rate on dynamic booth pricing as KATE targets Q1 2027 launch
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Nextech3D.AI Corporation (NEXCF) Q2 2027

Management View

  • "Nextech is accelerating. This is now our second consecutive quarter of 100% year-over-year revenue growth." (Founder, CEO & Chairman Evan Gappelberg)
  • "Our Event Tech business grew even faster, increasing 113% year-over-year and 50% sequentially." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • "From January 1 through September, we saw 180 new customers representing more than $1 million in new contract value, including for the first time ever multiyear enterprise agreements." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • "We are no longer simply an event tech company. We're building an AI-first technology company with the ability to serve multiple markets through a growing portfolio of integrated solutions." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • "We are rebranding as Nextech AI Technologies, which will be subject to approval at our next Annual General Meeting." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • "At the center...of this strategy...is what we're calling Nextech One. It's our unified customer-facing tech platform." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • "Revenue increased approximately 100% year-over-year to $779,000, while gross profit increased 98% to $678,000." (CFO Anum Waqas)
  • "We reported a net loss of approximately $591,000 for the quarter. However, approximately $533,000 of that loss was noncash stock-based compensation." (CFO Waqas)

Outlook

  • "With KATE, we've expanded into AI-powered workforce training, compliance, and knowledge management, which is going to be launching in Q1 2027." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • "We're now moving into self-serve markets that are quite substantial, including festivals and farmers markets." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • "We have no plans to raise any additional capital." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • The transcript did not include quarterly revenue or EPS guidance ranges, and the analysts estimates JSON was empty, so no estimates comparison was possible.

Financial Results

  • "Our gross margin reached 87% compared with 80% in Q1." (CFO Waqas)
  • "Excluding approximately $533,000 in noncash stock-based compensation, our adjusted net loss for the quarter would have been just $59,000." (CFO Waqas)
  • "Subsequent to the quarter end, we closed a $720,000 private placement with Evan and I participating through associates for around $350,000 combined, representing over half of the offerings." (CFO Waqas)
  • "We remain focused on improving liquidity through revenue growth, collections, and disciplined cost management." (CFO Waqas)

Q&A

  • Unknown Executive: How many quarters of runway and what is the outlook on breakeven and further dilution after the $720,000 placement? CEO Gappelberg: "We have no plans to raise any additional capital."
  • Unknown Executive: How much of the $1 million in new contract value was recognized in Q2 vs. deferred revenue, and what take rate is expected from dynamic pricing? CEO Gappelberg: "For incremental revenue, we're going to get 30% and our customer will get 70%...That's the take rate." CEO Gappelberg added on contract value timing: "I'll have to get back to you on how much of that is deferred and how much was in Q2."
  • Mark: Given many large enterprises have training systems, will KATE target smaller companies, and how does KATE learn? CEO Gappelberg: "All those training manuals...get fed into KATE...And then as you continuously interact with her, she learns and gets smarter and smarter and smarter."
  • Alan: How should investors view cash flow breakeven given prior commentary and current direction? CEO Gappelberg: "It's very hard to point your finger at the exact moment in time that we pop into cash flow positive" and "it's really a little premature to start talking about the moment in time that we're going to be going cash flow positive."
  • Steve: What is the status of the multimillion-dollar contract announced in August? CEO Gappelberg: "It has not closed...I'm not going to talk about it anymore other than to say it didn't close."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts/investors (as submitted questions) were slightly negative, concentrating on dilution, cash runway, revenue recognition vs. deferred revenue, and breakeven timing, including the direct question on "cash runway and dilution" and the follow-up on "cash flow breakeven."
  • Management tone was positive in prepared remarks and more guarded in Q&A on financing, contract timing, and profitability, including "We have no plans to raise any additional capital" and "it's really a little premature" regarding cash flow positive timing.
  • A prior-quarter sentiment comparison was not possible because the previous-quarter transcript was not provided beyond a "not available" placeholder.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The previous-quarter transcript was not available in the prompt, so management guidance language shifts, metric changes, and Q&A theme changes versus last quarter could not be verified or quoted.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Enterprise sales is a tricky business...Not every deal is going to close." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • "That multimillion dollar contract is out there...It has not closed." (CEO Gappelberg)
  • On profitability timing, CEO Gappelberg cautioned that the company is still investing: "As of today, we're still building that foundational layer."
  • On corporate actions, CEO Gappelberg stated: "ARway is closed. We're just waiting for regulatory approval before we can announce it."

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized two consecutive quarters of 100% year-over-year revenue growth alongside an 87% gross margin, while positioning Nextech One as the unified platform strategy and describing AI features such as dynamic booth pricing with a "30%" incremental-revenue take rate. The company also highlighted a planned Q1 2027 launch for KATE’s workforce training and compliance product, stated "no plans" for additional capital raises, and acknowledged that an announced multimillion-dollar contract "has not closed," while describing enterprise sales as uneven by nature.

data.title: TechnipFMC secures up to $1.25B in Exxon Guyana contracts
data.description:
TechnipFMC (FTI) said post-market Thursday it was awarded two contracts by ExxonMobil (XOM) to supply subsea systems for the Longtail development in Guyana's Stabroek Block.

TechnipFMC (FTI) said the "large" contract, valued in the $500M-$1B range, covers project management, engineering, and manufacturing of a full subsea production system; the subsea architecture includes Subsea 2.0 trees, manifolds, and associated controls for the gas condensate development.

The separate "significant" contract, valued in the $75M-$250M range, covers the design and manufacture of flexible production risers for the Longtail development; the company said it will provide the same riser solution that was utilized on the Yellowtail and Payara phases of the Stabroek development.

TechnipFMC (FTI) said Longtail is its eighth greenfield project working together with Exxon (XOM).

data.title: TPG, Corpay to take BILL private in $6B acquisition
data.description:
• BILL (BILL) said on Thursday that it has entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, a leading global alternative asset management firm, in partnership with Corpay (CPAY) for $6B.
  • BILL will receive $63.25 per share in an all-cash transaction, representing a 31% premium to the 60-day volume-weighted average price ending on November 16.
  • TPG will acquire a majority interest in BILL through TPG Capital, the firm’s U.S. and European private equity platform, and Corpay will acquire a minority interest.
  • Upon the close of the transaction, BILL will become a privately held company, and its common stock will no longer be listed on any public stock exchange.
  • BILL -3.25% to $62.00.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Foremost Clean Energy names Chang as new President/CEO
data.description:
Foremost Clean Energy (FMST) said post-market Thursday it appointed Rob Chang as its new President and CEO, bringing nearly 30 years of experience in mining and natural resources, capital markets, institutional investing, and public-company leadership to his new leadership role.

Chang was co-founder and CEO of Gryphon Digital Mining, which he led through a Nasdaq listing and subsequent merger with American Bitcoin, and he was Managing Director and Head of Metals and Mining at Cantor Fitzgerald, where he provided research coverage in precious metals, base metals, lithium, and uranium.

David Cates, who served as Foremost's (FMST) interim President and CEO, will resume his role as an independent member of its board; he also serves as full-time CEO of Denison Mines, Foremost's largest shareholder.

data.title: New Zealand Energy launches C$3M private placement, targets oil growth
data.description:
• New Zealand Energy (NZ:CA) announced on Thursday a C$3M private placement at C$0.35 per share to fund its gas storage project, oil well interventions, and general working capital.
  • The offering is expected to close around November 30, subject to regulatory approvals.
  • The company plans to increase oil production by more than 800 barrels per day through well maintenance and upgrades over the next few months.
  • Its Tariki 1A well continues to produce approximately 2.5 MMcf/d of gas, with a 50% working interest held by the company
  • CEO Toby Pierce said the company is advancing its gas storage project while prioritizing oil production growth.

data.title: Calif. AG serves Nvidia investigative subpoena over China issues
data.description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia (NVDA) related to former CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese operative.

The California Department of Justice plans to investigate if Nvidia misled investors regarding whether its advanced GPUs or confidential information made it to China.

"The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," Bonta said. "My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information—and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law. Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation, but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: companies cannot mislead their investors."
